author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: La thoh ïa kane ka kot kat kum ki ktienrim bad 'tien tymmen katba lah ban kynmaw bad ban shem mynta na ki ktien jong phi.
english: This book has been written according to ancient words and traditional proverbs as much as can be remembered and found today from your own spoken language.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ban shu pyllait lymbiang ïa kane ka kot Niam tip-Blei tip-Briew donsot donkular ki Khasi, nga sngew sah pap halor lade.
english: To neglect publishing this book on the Khasi religion of knowing God and knowing humankind, righteousness and covenant, I feel sin remaining upon myself.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Mynta ki khun Khasi jong ngi kim don jingïahikai jingïapule shuh shaphang ka Hok ka sot ha la ïing la ïing kumba don ha kibarim.
english: Today our Khasi children no longer receive home instruction and learning regarding Truth and Righteousness as existed among the ancestors.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ha shnong ruh kim don tymmen shuh ki ban sneng ban kraw shnong kumba ju don mynno mynno.
english: In the villages too, there are no longer elders to counsel and guide the village community as was customary in bygone days.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: U Khasi u ngeit ba u briew u wan sha kane ka pyrthei tang ban kamai ïa ka Hok.
english: The Khasi believes that man comes into this earthly world solely to earn Righteousness.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ka Hok ka long ka nongrim jong ka jingim briew baroh kawei.
english: Righteousness is the bedrock foundation of all human life.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Lada u briew u duh ïa ka Hok, u duh ïa ka jingim bad ïa ka burom ha khmat U Blei.
english: If a person loses Righteousness, they lose life and honour before the face of God.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ban kamai ïa ka Hok kam mut tang ka jingkylla spah, hynrei ka jinglong babha ha ka jingim.
english: To earn Righteousness does not mean acquiring material riches, but cultivating virtue and moral uprightness in life.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ka Niam Khasi ka dei ka Niam Tip-Briew Tip-Blei.
english: The Khasi religion is the faith of Knowing Humankind and Knowing God.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ym lah ban tip ïa U Blei lada ym da tip shwa ban burom bad sngewthuh ïa u briew.
english: One cannot know God unless one first learns to respect and understand fellow human beings.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: U Blei u Nongbuh Nongthaw u don ha ki bynta baroh jong ka mariang bad ka jingthaw.
english: God the Sovereign Creator is present across all realms of nature and creation.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: U Blei u ym don dur don dar, hynrei u don ka bor bad ka jingshai kaba khraw.
english: God possesses no physical form or idol, yet possesses infinite power and great divine light.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ka jinglong Khasi ka shong ha ka Tip-Kur Tip-Kha.
english: Khasi identity and social order reside fundamentally in Knowing Maternal Kin and Paternal Relations.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: U Kur u dei u kpa-tymmen na ka liang ka kmie, bad u Kha u dei na ka liang u kpa.
english: The Kur constitutes the maternal clan from the mother's lineage, while Kha stems from the father's side.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Uba kheiñ-kur kheiñ-kha u long uba don akor bad uba don niam ha ka imlang sahlang.
english: He who honours matrilineal clan and paternal relations is recognized as courteous and pious in society.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ka shongkha kur ka long ka sang kaba khraw tam kaba pynjot ïa ka jaidbynriew.
english: Endogamous marriage within the maternal clan is the gravest taboo and mortal sacrilege destroying the tribe.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: U Blei u la buh ïa ka jutang bad u briew mynba u thaw ïa u ha pyrthei.
english: God established a divine covenant with man at the very dawn when He created him upon earth.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Kane ka jutang ka long ka ktien kaba u briew u la kular ban bat ha la ka rynieng.
english: This covenant represents the sacred pledge that humankind vowed to uphold throughout mortal existence.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Haba u briew u pynkheiñ ïa kane ka kular, ka sang bad ka ma ki wan ban tyllep ïa u.
english: Whenever man violates this covenant, severe ritual taboos and peril descend to engulf him.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ka daw kaba pynjot ïa ka jinglong tymmen long san ka dei ka jinglait ktien bad jingshim kabu.
english: The underlying cause that ruins venerable traditions is breach of word and moral exploitation.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ki Khasi ki kheiñ kyntang ïa ki khlaw kiba ki khot ki Law Kyntang bad Law Adong.
english: The Khasis regard as holy and sacred certain forest groves designated as Law Kyntang and Law Adong.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ym bit ban kheit syntiew, ban thoh dieng, lane ban pynjot ïa kawei ruh ka shynrain ha Law Kyntang.
english: It is forbidden to pluck flowers, fell trees, or harm a single dry twig within the Sacred Grove.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: U Ryngkew u Basa u sumar ïa ki khlaw bad ïa ki tyllong um jong ka shnong.
english: The guardian spirits Ryngkew and Basa protect the sacred forests and the village headwaters.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ki ummat jong ka mariang ki kyrsoi na ki lum ban pyndap ïa ki wah duid bad ki wah bah.
english: The pristine waters of mother nature spring from the hills to replenish streams and mighty rivers.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Haba u Khasi u duwai, u kren ha ka ktien ba khuid khlem jingphikier ne jingshukor.
english: When a Khasi offers prayer, he speaks in pure language without hypocrisy or deceit.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ka nguh ka dem ka long ka jingpynphai khmat sha U Blei Uba Lah Ban Leh Baroh.
english: Humble adoration and bowing represent turning one's face toward Almighty God.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: U Syiem u dei u khlieh jong ka Hima, hynrei u dei tang u nongsumar ba la bynshet da ki paidbah.
english: The Syiem is the political head of the realm, yet serves merely as a custodian entrusted by the people.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ki Myntri bad ki Bakhraw ki ïa shong dorbar ban rai halor ki kam shnong kam hima.
english: The customary Ministers and Nobles sit in assembly council to deliberate on civic affairs of state.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: U Maw-shynrang u ïeng pyrshah ïa ka sngi bad ka Maw-kynthei ka thiah pynkiang kum ka synduk.
english: The upright male stone stands facing the sun, while the flat female dolmen stone rests horizontally like a cist.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Kine ki maw kim dei ki blei, hynrei ki dei tang ki dak kynmaw ïa ka burom jong ka kur.
english: These monoliths are not deities worshipped, but enduring historical monuments commemorating the lineage honour of the maternal clan.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ka jingbuh mawbah ka pynïasoh lang ïa ki shyieng jong ka kur baroh hapoh kawei ka ling maw.
english: The final internment under the clan ossuary (Mawbah) unites the bones of all clan kin within a single stone sepulchre.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Haba la poi ka por ban buh mawbah, ka kur baroh ka wan khot ban ïa don bynta ha ka niam.
english: When the auspicious time arrives to inter remains in the clan ossuary, the entire clan is summoned to participate in the solemn rites.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
section: Life Cycle: Ka Jer Ka Thoh
khasi: Lada u dei u shynrang ki buh ïa ka ryntieh bad ki khnam, lada ka dei ka kynthei ki buh ïa ka khoh bad u star.
english: If the babe be a boy they place a bow and arrows, while if a girl they place the conical basket (khoh) and woven headstrap (star).

author: U Sib Charan Roy
section: Life Cycle: Ka Jer Ka Thoh
khasi: Ka ryntieh bad ki khnam ki thew ba un long u rangbah u ban ïada ïa ka kur bad ka hima.
english: The bow and arrows symbolize that he shall grow into a valiant warrior defender shielding clan and kingdom.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
section: Life Cycle: Ka Jer Ka Thoh
khasi: Ka khoh bad u star ki thew ba kan long ka nongri-ïing bad ka nongkamai spah jong ka ïing.
english: The conical basket and headstrap symbolize that she shall be the industrious keeper of hearth and domestic steward.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ha ka shongkurim, u kñi jong ka kynthei bad u kñi jong u shynrang ki ïakren ban pynskhem ïa ka jutang.
english: In solemn marriage matrimony, the maternal uncle of the bride and that of the groom negotiate to establish the sacred covenant.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: U tnga u wan shong ha ïing ka tnga kumba long ka dustur matrilocal jong ka jaidbynriew.
english: The husband takes up residence in the home of the bride in keeping with the ancient matrilocal matrilineal custom of the people.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Haba u briew u ïap, ki ong ba u la leit bam kwai ha ïing U Blei.
english: When a virtuous person passes away, the Khasis say that they have gone to partake of betel nut in the celestial House of God.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ka mynsiem kam ju ïap, hynrei ka leit phai biang sha U Nongthaw Uba la ai ïa ka.
english: The immortal human spirit never perishes, but returns home to the Supreme Creator who bestowed breath upon it.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Uba im ha ka pap bad ka sang un sa shah pynshitom bad un ym ïoh rung ha ka burom U Blei.
english: He who lived immersed in mortal sin and taboo shall endure spiritual affliction and be barred from entering divine glory.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Haba nga ïaid lyngba ka ri khlaw jong kane ka pyrthei, nga la poi ha kawei ka jaka kaba don ka krem.
english: As I walked through the wilderness of this world, I lighted on a certain place where was a den.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Nga la thiah ha kata ka jaka ban shongthait, bad haba nga la ïohthiah nga la phohsniew.
english: I laid me down in that place to sleep; and, as I slept, I dreamed a dream.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Ha kata ka jingphohsniew nga la ïohi ïa uwei u briew uba da kup da ki jaiñ jot.
english: I dreamed, and behold, I saw a man clothed with rags.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U ïeng bad ka khmat jong u ka phai sha lyndet na la ka jong ka ïing.
english: Standing in a certain place, with his face turned away from his own house.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Nga la khmih bad nga la ïohi ba u la plied ïa kata ka kot bad u la pule ha ka.
english: I looked, and saw him open the book and read therein.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Katba u dang pule u la ïam bad u la khynñiuh da ka jingsheptieng.
english: And, as he read, he wept, and trembled with exceeding fear.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U khlem lah shuh ban theh lade, bad u la pyrta da ka sur kaba sngewsih, Kaei ngan leh?
english: Unable longer to contain himself, he broke out with a lamentable cry, saying, What shall I do?

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U la leit phai sha la ka ïing, hynrei um lah shuh ban buhrieh ïa la ka jingsngewsih na la ka tnga bad ki khun.
english: In this plight, therefore, he went home to his house, but could not long conceal his sorrow from his wife and children.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: La pyntip ha nga ba kane ka shnong jong ngi kan sa shah bam ha ka ding na bneng.
english: Moreover, I am certainly informed that this our city will be burned with fire from heaven.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Haba ki la ïohsngew ïa kine ki ktien, ki la pyrkhat ba ka khlieh jong u ka la shit noh.
english: At this his relations were sore amazed, thinking some frenzy distemper had got into his head.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Mar ïa ong kumta, nga la ïohi ïa uwei u briew uba kyrteng U Nongiathuhkhana uba la wan ha u.
english: Now, as he was walking in the fields, behold, a man named Evangelist came to him.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U la kylli ïa u, Balei me ïam bad me pyrta kumne?
english: And asked him, Wherefore dost thou weep and cry?

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U Nongiathuhkhana u la ai ha u ïa kawei ka kot kaba thoh, Phet na ka jingbitar kaban sa wan!
english: Then Evangelist gave him a parchment roll, and there was written within, Flee from the wrath to come!

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U briew u la kylli, Shano ngan phet?
english: The man therefore read it, and looking upon Evangelist very carefully, said, Whither must I fly?

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U Nongiathuhkhana u la kdew da ka shynriahti, Me ïohi ïatai ka khyrdop ba rit sha jngai?
english: Then said Evangelist, pointing with his finger over a very wide field, Do you see yonder Wicket-gate?

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U briew u la ong, Em, ngam ïohi bha, hynrei nga ïohi ïa ka jingshai kaba phyrnai.
english: The man said, No, I do not see it; but methinks I see a shining light.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Katba ki dang ïaid lyngba ka madan, ki la poi harud kawei ka ktieh kaba jur kaba kyrteng Ka Bir Jingduh-Jingkyrmen.
english: Now, as they drew near, they drew towards a miry slough that was in the midst of the plain, the name of which was Despond.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Ki la ngam shapoh jong ka khlem da kheiñ, namar kim shym la phikir ïa la ki kjat.
english: And being heedless, they did both fall suddenly into the bog.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U Pilgrim u la ngam kham jylliew namar kata ka jingkit kaba khia kaba don halor ka met jong u.
english: Here Christian began to sink in the mire, because of the great burden that was on his back.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Hynrei uwei u briew uba kyrteng U Nongïarap u la wan bad u la shim ïa ka kti jong u ban ring ïa u na kata ka ktieh.
english: Then I saw in my dream, that a man came to him, whose name was Help, and took him by the hand and drew him out.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U Pilgrim u la kiew shaphrang haduh ba u la poi ha uwei u lum uba don ka Diengphna halor jong u.
english: He ran thus till he came at a place somewhat ascending; and upon that place stood a Cross.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Mar ïa poi u ha khmat kata ka Diengphna, kata ka jingkit ka la dkut bad ka la tyllun noh na ka met jong u.
english: So I saw in my dream, that just as Christian came up with the Cross, his burden loosed from off his shoulders.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Ka la tyllun shapoh kawei ka jingtep kaba jylliew, bad um shym la ïohi shuh ïa ka.
english: And fell from off his back, and began to tumble, and so continued to do till it came to the mouth of the sepulchre, where it fell in, and I saw it no more.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Te u Pilgrim u la kmen shibun eh bad u la shad da ka jingkmen ha la ka dohnud.
english: Then was Christian glad and lightsome, and said with a merry heart, He hath given me rest by his sorrow.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Ha kata ka miet u la poi ha kawei ka ïingkham kaba bhabriew kaba don harud ka lynti.
english: So I saw in my dream that he made haste and went forward, and came to the Palace Beautiful by the highway side.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Ki samla kynthei kiba kyrteng Ka Jingstad, Ka Jingakorbha, bad Ka Jingieit ki la pdiang sngewbha ïa u.
english: The fair maidens Piety, Prudence, and Charity opened the doors and welcomed him in.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Ki la ai ha u ïa ki jaiñ-riam thma kiba kynthup ïa ka stieh jong ka jingngeit bad ka waitlam jong ka ktien.
english: They led him into the armoury, and showed him all manner of weapons: the shield of faith and the sword of the spirit.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Haba u la hiar sha ka Them Sngewrit, u la ïashem bad uwei u ksuid uba shyrkhei uba kyrteng U Apollyon.
english: In the Valley of Humiliation, poor Christian was hard put to it; for he had gone but a little way before he espied a foul fiend coming to meet him, named Apollyon.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Hynrei u Pilgrim u la bat skhem ïa la ka waitlam bad u la pyndonkam ïa ka stieh ban ïada ïa lade.
english: Christian nimbly drew his sword and caught the shield, making noble defence against the darts of the dragon.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Hadien ka jingïaleh kaba jur, u Apollyon u la phet noh bad u la iehnoh ïa u ha ka jingsuk.
english: With that Apollyon spread forth his dragon wings, and sped him away, that Christian for a season saw him no more.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Hadien kane ki la poi ha kawei ka shnong kaba don ka ïew kaba heh kaba kyrteng Ka Ïew Kai-kam.
english: Almost as soon as they were got out of the wilderness, they saw a town before them, named Vanity; and at that town there is a fair kept, called Vanity Fair.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Ha kata ka ïew la die ïa ki jingthala baroh: ka spah, ka nam, ka burom, bad ki jinglehbyrngia jong kane ka pyrthei.
english: At this fair are all such merchandise sold as houses, lands, trades, places, honours, preferments, titles, and all kinds of worldly delights.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U Faithful u la ïeng skhem ha la ka jingngeit bad u la shah pynïap noh da ka jingthang ha ka ding ha khmat ki briew.
english: Faithful stood fast in his confession of truth and was condemned to be burned to ashes at the stake before the angry mob.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Hynrei kawei ka kali ksiar ka la wan ban shim ïa u Faithful beit sha ka Shnong Bneng.
english: Now I saw that there stood behind the multitude a chariot and a couple of horses waiting for Faithful, which carried him up straight through the clouds to the celestial gate.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Katba ki dang ïaid lyngba ka madan By-path, ki la thiah ha u phlang bad la kem ïa ki da u Riewkhraw Jingduh-Jingkyrmen.
english: Now, a little before them there was a stile, and they fell asleep; and Giant Despair, walking in his fields, caught them trespassing upon his grounds.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U la ring ïa ki sha la ka Kut kaba dum bad u la thep ïa ki ha ka patok kaba jylliew bad ba sma.
english: He therefore drove them before him, and put them into his castle, into a very dark dungeon, nasty and stinking to the spirits of these two men.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Da kata ka shabi ki la plied ïa ki jingkhang baroh jong kata ka kut bad ki la phet lait ha ka jingsuk.
english: Then Christian pulled it out of his bosom, and turned the lock, and the door flew open with ease, and they escaped swiftly into the King's highway.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Ki la kiew halor ki Lum Bhabriew bad ki la khmih sha jngai ïa ka kynroh jong ka Shnong Bneng.
english: Then they went up into the Delectable Mountains to behold the gardens and orchards, and looked through the perspective glass toward the Celestial City.

source_book: Ki Dienjat Jong Ki Longshwa & Kot Pule
author: Traditional Oral Lore / Babu Jeebon Roy
khasi: Hyndai hinthai, halor u Lum Diengiei la mih uwei u dieng uba khraw tam ha ka pyrthei.
english: In ancient mythical times, atop the peak of Diengiei Mountain grew the greatest colossal tree in the world.

source_book: Ki Dienjat Jong Ki Longshwa & Kot Pule
author: Traditional Oral Lore / Babu Jeebon Roy
khasi: Uta u dieng u la san ha ka rynieng kaba jrong haduh ban da kah dum ïa ka sngi bad ka pyrthei baroh kawei.
english: That sacred tree grew to such towering height that its canopy cast total darkness over the sun and the whole earth.

source_book: Ki Dienjat Jong Ki Longshwa & Kot Pule
author: Traditional Oral Lore / Babu Jeebon Roy
khasi: Ki briew bad ki mrad baroh ki la ïashem shitom namar ym don jingshai shuh ban im.
english: Both human beings and animals suffered greatly because there was no longer sunlight to sustain living things.

source_book: Ki Dienjat Jong Ki Longshwa & Kot Pule
author: Traditional Oral Lore / Babu Jeebon Roy
khasi: Haba ki la kylli na ka Sim Phreit, ka la bthah ba ki dei ban buh ki sdie ba khlem pat pynkhuid ha kata ka thliew.
english: When they consulted the little Wren bird (Sim Phreit), she revealed that they must leave sharp axes sticking blade-outward into the trunk cuts.

source_book: Ki Dienjat Jong Ki Longshwa & Kot Pule
author: Traditional Oral Lore / Babu Jeebon Roy
khasi: Kumta uta u dieng u la kyllon, bad ka jingshai jong ka sngi ka la wan phyrnai biang halor ka pyrthei.
english: Thus the immense tree finally toppled, and the golden radiance of the sun shone down once again across the earth.

source_book: Ki Dienjat Jong Ki Longshwa & Kot Pule
author: Traditional Oral Lore / Babu Jeebon Roy
khasi: U Lum Sohpetbneng u long u lum uba kyntang tam ha ka niam bad ka jutang jong ki Khasi.
english: Sohpetbneng Peak is the most sacred navel mountain in the religion and spiritual covenant of the Khasi people.

source_book: Ki Dienjat Jong Ki Longshwa & Kot Pule
author: Traditional Oral Lore / Babu Jeebon Roy
khasi: Khat-hynriew trep ki shong ha bneng, bad ki hynñiew trep ki la hiar ban shong ban sah ha pyrthei.
english: Sixteen celestial families dwelt in heaven, and the Seven Huts (Ki Hynñiew Trep) descended to inhabit and cultivate the earth.

source_book: Ki Dienjat Jong Ki Longshwa & Kot Pule
author: Traditional Oral Lore / Babu Jeebon Roy
khasi: Ki briew ki ju kiew bad hiar man ka sngi ban ïasyllok bad U Blei Nongthaw ha ka jingsuk.
english: People freely ascended and descended daily to commune directly with God the Creator in unbroken peace.

source_book: Ki Dienjat Jong Ki Longshwa & Kot Pule
author: Traditional Oral Lore / Babu Jeebon Roy
khasi: Hynrei namar ka pop bad ka jingkhwan jong u briew, kata ka jingkieng ksiar ka la dkut noh shi junom.
english: Yet owing to human transgression and greedy arrogance, that golden bridge was severed forevermore.

source_book: Ki Dienjat Jong Ki Longshwa & Kot Pule
author: Traditional Oral Lore / Babu Jeebon Roy
khasi: Miet man ka miet u ju tem ïa la ka sharati halor ka lyngwiar dpei da ka sur kaba pynjaw-ummat.
english: Night after night he played his mournful melodies over the hearth ashes with notes that moved the heavens to tears.

source_book: Ki Dienjat Jong Ki Longshwa & Kot Pule
author: Traditional Oral Lore / Babu Jeebon Roy
khasi: Ka Mahadei jong u Syiem ka la ïohsngew ïa kata ka sur bad ka la shah thap ha ka jingieit ba la khang.
english: The Queen of the reigning Syiem heard that haunting song and was drawn into forbidden and tragic love.

source_book: Ki Dienjat Jong Ki Longshwa & Kot Pule
author: Traditional Oral Lore / Babu Jeebon Roy
khasi: Haba la shem ïa ka jingshisha, u Manik u la mih ban pdiang ïa la ka kuna da kaba thang lade ha ka ding.
english: When the truth was revealed, Manik stepped forth with dignity to accept divine judgment by casting himself into the funeral pyre.

source_book: Ki Dienjat Jong Ki Longshwa & Kot Pule
author: Traditional Oral Lore / Babu Jeebon Roy
khasi: U Thlen u ju bam briew bad u dawa ba ki briew ki dei ban ai snam briew man ka por ban pynsuk ïa u.
english: The Thlen devoured human flesh and demanded human blood sacrifice from evil keepers to grant ill-gotten wealth.

source_book: Ki Dienjat Jong Ki Longshwa & Kot Pule
author: Traditional Oral Lore / Babu Jeebon Roy
khasi: Uwei u rangbah uba shlur uba kyrteng U Suidnoh u la thaw lad ban pynïap noh ïa une u bsein ba sniew.
english: A brave warrior youth named U Suidnoh devised an ingenious stratagem to destroy this malevolent monstrous serpent.

source_book: Ki Dienjat Jong Ki Longshwa & Kot Pule
author: Traditional Oral Lore / Babu Jeebon Roy
khasi: U la ai bam da u nar ba la sait shit phyrnai ha ka shyntur jong u thlen haduh ba un da ïap.
english: He fed the ravenous monster red-hot glowing iron tongs thrust down its throat until it perished in agony.

source_book: Ki Dienjat Jong Ki Longshwa & Kot Pule
author: Traditional Oral Lore / Babu Jeebon Roy
khasi: Na kata ka daw, ka jingkheinduh jong u thlen ka la sah pateng kum ka jingngeit ha ki bynta jong ka ri.
english: Consequently, the dark superstition of the Thlen persisted across generations as a dreaded folklore belief in the land.

source_book: Ki Dienjat Jong Ki Longshwa & Kot Pule
author: Traditional Oral Lore / Babu Jeebon Roy
section: Folktale: Ka Sngi bad U Bnai
khasi: Hyndai ka Sngi bad u Bnai ki long shi para ba shong lang ha bneng.
english: In primeval antiquity, the Sun and the Moon were sister and brother dwelling together harmoniously in the heavens.

source_book: Ki Dienjat Jong Ki Longshwa & Kot Pule
author: Traditional Oral Lore / Babu Jeebon Roy
section: Folktale: Ka Sngi bad U Bnai
khasi: Ka Sngi ka long ka para kynthei kaba bhabriew, bad u Bnai u dei u hynmen shynrang uba don ka mynsiem ba sniew.
english: The Sun was the radiant younger sister, while the Moon was the elder brother harboring unseemly wicked desires.

source_book: Ki Dienjat Jong Ki Longshwa & Kot Pule
author: Traditional Oral Lore / Babu Jeebon Roy
section: Folktale: Ka Sngi bad U Bnai
khasi: Naduh kata ka sngi, ka khmat jong u Bnai ka la sah dum bad thoh-dak kumba ngi ïohi mynta ha sahit bneng.
english: Ever since that fateful day, the face of the Moon remained permanently darkened and crater-stained across the night sky.
